readme.en:
Infrared Is Not Dead. Your Homey Proves It. Get your IR to the next level.

Infrared is the most widely used wireless protocol for home appliances on the planet, and probably the most overlooked one as well.
This app brings back the feature I missed the most after it was removed: triggering flows with your IR remote.  Because it is so much easier than the alternatives. I turn on the TV, and Homey automatically switches the HiFi to the right input, dims the lights and closes the blinds. No reaching for the phone, no unlocking it, no finding the app or a widget, no starting a flow by hand, and no arguing with Siri, Alexa or any of the other ladies. I also programmed one of the spare buttons on my remote to trigger the full sleep flow. The best automation is the kind you trigger without even thinking about it.

FEATURES
•  Learn mode: point a remote at Homey, press a button, and the signal is captured and verified. Press the same button again to confirm. Finetune it.
•  Manual entry: Paste a code in Pronto Hex, HEX, Global Caché, Broadlink or the native Homey format.
•  IR database: Global Caché keeps an online database with more than 285,000 codes. Look one up and enter it by hand.
•  Single command or full remote: Add one button, or build a remote with several named, iconised commands such as power, volume, navigation and playback.
•  Custom icons
•  Quick on/off button: Map two commands to a single on/off toggle.
•  Advanced view: inspect the pulse graph, carrier, hex value, bit length and pulse/gap timings of any captured signal.
•  Toggle-bit handling for RC5 and RC6, so both variants of a keypress are recognised.
•  Trigger flows: a learned infrared signal can start a Homey flow.
•  Action flows: Send out recorded or manually entered codes

HARDWARE
You need a pre-2023 Homey to receive signals and to trigger flows with infrared. The 2023 and later models do not have IR receivers. However they do have IR transmitters so you can still add infrared signals manually and send them.
This means the "old" Homeys just went up in value if you care about IR. Long live the classics.
Practical tip: if IR reception matters to you, turn off the LED ring on your pre-2023 Homey. It can cause interference, and learning works noticeably better with the ring dark.

SUPPORTED PROTOCOLS AND CARRIER FREQUENCIES
NEC 38 kHz
Sony SIRC 40 kHz
Samsung 38 kHz
JVC 38 kHz
Panasonic 37 kHz
RC5 36 kHz
RC6 (mode 0) 36 kHz
RC6 (mode 6A) 36 kHz
Generic (raw) 38 kHz, up to 128 bits

The app has been tested with RC5 and RC6 (Philips remotes). Homey turned out to be more responsive to infrared than my own devices also the signals sent out by homey are stronger than my remotes.

NON-SUPPORTED PROTOCOLS AND LIMITATIONS
The infrared world is more complex than it looks, so do not be surprised if a number of remotes will not work. Typical examples that are out of scope:	
•  Sharp and Denon coding, which uses a very different timing structure.
•  Mitsubishi, Toshiba and RCA code formats.
•  Cisco and other 56/57 kHz systems. Carriers far outside roughly 30 to 45 kHz are not handled.
•  Bang & Olufsen, which uses a 455 kHz carrier, and similar exotic hardware.
•  Air conditioners that send one very long state frame (temperature, mode and fan speed all at once), such as Daikin, Fujitsu, Mitsubishi, Midea and Toshiba. Those frames are simply too  long for Homey to handle.

description.en: Get your InfraRed to the next level

titleFormatted.en: Any IR signal received with sensitivity [[sensitivity]]

hint.en: Triggers when Homey receives an infrared signal. Sensitivity has a permitted range of 0.0 to 0.5. A value of 0.0 is strictest, 0.5 is most lenient and 0.4 is the default. Below 0.3, signals only caught by the generic profile are ignored.

Triggers when Homey receives the IR command stored on this device. Sensitivity has a permitted range of 0.0 to 0.5. A value of 0.0 only accepts the exact stored code from the same protocol, 0.5 is most lenient and 0.3 is the default. The RC5 and RC6 toggle bit never counts as a difference.
Sends any supported infrared code. Repetitions default to 10 and use a permitted range of 1 to 255. For alternating RC5 or RC6 toggle frames, use the RC5 or RC6 action card.

titleFormatted.en: Send [[code_type]] code [[code]] with [[repeat]] repetitions for [[toggle]] toggle frames

hint.en: Only accepts an RC5 or RC6 code with a recognised toggle bit. Repetitions default to 10 for each frame. Toggle count defaults to 1. A toggle count of 4 sends toggle 0, toggle 1, toggle 0 and toggle 1.
Sends a stored command. Repetitions default to 10 and use a permitted range of 1 to 255. For alternating RC5 or RC6 toggle frames, use the stored RC5 or RC6 action card.

title.en: Send stored RC5 or RC6 code

titleFormatted.en: Send [[command]] with [[repeat]] repetitions for [[toggle]] toggle frames

hint.en: Only lists stored RC5 or RC6 commands with a recognised toggle bit. Repetitions default to 10 for each frame. Toggle count defaults to 1. A toggle count of 4 sends toggle 0, toggle 1, toggle 0 and toggle 1.

readme.en:
Bring your motorcycle or scooter into your smart home. See at a glance whether it is parked or on the road, and let your home respond when you ride off, park, come home or when the theft alarm goes off.

Log in with your Komobi Moto account and add every vehicle in your garage as its own device. Everyone in your home can add the vehicles of their own Komobi account: you log in each time you add vehicles. Each vehicle shows whether it is parked or riding, the theft alarm, the battery of the tracker, the vehicle and the key fob, the odometer, its location and how far it is from home.

Use the flow cards to act when your vehicle starts riding or parks, when the theft alarm goes off or is switched on or off, when it arrives home or leaves, when the vehicle or key fob battery runs low, when you leave your key fob behind, or when Komobi stores a new ride with its distance, duration, speed and driving score.

Add the vehicle status widget to your dashboard to see the status of a vehicle at a glance.

This app is not made by or affiliated with Komobi. It uses the same online service as the Komobi Moto app, so your vehicle needs an active Komobi subscription.
readme.nl:
Haal je motor of scooter je slimme huis in. Zie in één oogopslag of hij geparkeerd staat of onderweg is, en laat je huis reageren als je wegrijdt, parkeert, thuiskomt of als het diefstalalarm afgaat.

Log in met je Komobi Moto account en voeg elk voertuig uit je garage toe als een eigen apparaat. Iedereen in huis kan de voertuigen van zijn eigen Komobi account toevoegen: je logt in elke keer dat je voertuigen toevoegt. Per voertuig zie je of het geparkeerd staat of rijdt, het diefstalalarm, de batterij van de tracker, de accu van het voertuig en de batterij van de sleutelhanger, de kilometerstand, de locatie en hoe ver het van huis is.

Gebruik de flowkaarten om iets te doen als je voertuig gaat rijden of parkeert, als het diefstalalarm afgaat of aan- of uitgezet wordt, als het thuiskomt of vertrekt, als de accu of de batterij van de sleutelhanger bijna leeg is, als je je sleutelhanger vergeet, of als Komobi een nieuwe rit opslaat met de afstand, duur, snelheid en rijscore.

Zet de voertuigstatus widget op je dashboard om de status van een voertuig in één oogopslag te zien.

Deze app is niet gemaakt door of verbonden aan Komobi. Hij gebruikt dezelfde online dienst als de Komobi Moto app, dus je voertuig heeft een actief Komobi abonnement nodig.

readme.en:
Read your Resol solar and heating controllers (DeltaSol MX, BS, SLT and many more) in Homey. The app connects locally to a KM2, DL2, DL3 or VBus/LAN module over your network. No cloud account is needed.

Add one device per controller, or one device per temperature sensor so you can place them in different rooms. Temperatures, pump speeds, irradiation, flow, operating hours and error status appear automatically. Use flow cards for value changes, errors, lost connection, and values above or below a threshold. Writing a value back to the controller is experimental and disabled by default.
readme.nl:
Lees je Resol zonne- en verwarmingsregelaars (DeltaSol MX, BS, SLT en vele andere) uit in Homey. De app maakt lokaal verbinding met een KM2, DL2, DL3 of VBus/LAN-module in je netwerk. Een cloudaccount is niet nodig.

Voeg per regelaar een apparaat toe, of per temperatuursensor zodat je ze in verschillende kamers kunt plaatsen. Temperaturen, pompsnelheden, instraling, doorstroming, bedrijfsuren en foutstatus verschijnen automatisch. Gebruik flowkaarten voor waardeveranderingen, fouten, verbroken verbinding en waarden boven of onder een grens. Een waarde terugschrijven naar de regelaar is experimenteel en standaard uitgeschakeld.

description.en: Read Resol solar and heating controllers (DeltaSol and others) via a KM2, DL2, DL3 or VBus/LAN adapter.
description.nl: Lees Resol zonne- en verwarmingsregelaars (DeltaSol e.a.) uit via een KM2, DL2, DL3 of VBus/LAN-adapter.

hint.en: Needs 'Allow writing' in device settings. Value ids are controller specific (see Resol docs).
hint.nl: Vereist 'Schrijven toestaan' in apparaatinstellingen. Value-id's zijn regelaarspecifiek (zie Resol-documentatie).

readme.en:
Connect your FreeKiosk Android kiosk to Homey to monitor and control it as part of your home automations. Keep common kiosk controls alongside your other Homey devices and use them in your everyday routines.

The live camera stream is available in the Homey mobile app, but not in the Homey Web App because FreeKiosk serves it as multipart/x-mixed-replace.
This application was entirely vibe-coded with AI assistance.
It does not yet implement every feature available in FreeKiosk; additional features can be added upon request.

description.en: Bring your Android kiosk into your smart home and keep everyday controls within reach.
